newsitem.title: UK: UK government defiant in ruling out EMU debate.
newsitem.headline: UK government defiant in ruling out EMU debate.

text.p: British government officials said on Friday that Prime Minister John Major still had no intention of bowing to pressure from rank and file Members of Parliament for a full-scale debate on economic and monetary union (EMU).
They said MPs would have an opportunity to express their views during the customary debate that will precede the European Union's Dublin summit next month.

Angry Conservative MPs deputed Sir Marcus Fox, chairman of their 1922 committee, to protest to Major at his refusal to allow a debate. Officials said they would meet early next week and the Prime Minister would listen carefully to what Fox said.
A senior governmet official said he had nothing add to what Major said yesterday in rejecting a debate on the floor of the House of Commons.
Major argued MPs had already been given a chance to scrutinise three working documents related to EMU in the committee set up for that purpose.
"The government is following perfectly normal procedures," he said.
The official denied reports that Major snubbed Fox by refusing to meet him last night. He said Fox had a dinner engagement.
